notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Proverbs 9 this time because my research tool stopped working before I read a single page. On my first try, the system said I had no more web searches or page fetches left for this turn, and a second try gave the same message. So I haven't read Enduring Word, the commentaries on Bible Hub (Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary, Wesley), Precept Austin, the NET Bible notes, or any of the other approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. I won't write commentary I can't source to a URL, so I haven't drafted anything.

Once the tool is available again, in a new message, I'll start with these pages:
- **Traditional readings:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/proverbs-9/, plus Bible Hub's Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary and Wesley pages for Proverbs 9, and Precept Austin's Proverbs 9 commentary.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** sermons and articles on Proverbs 9 on Ligonier, Desiring God, Seedbed and the Lutheran sites. Likely topics are reading wisdom's "house," "pillars" and "feast" as pointing to Christ or the Lord's Supper, and verse 10 on the fear of the Lord.
- **Other views:** the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship; New Advent for early Church writers on Wisdom's banquet; any material on the sites about prosperity readings of verse 11 ("your days will be multiplied").

To try again, just reply with "continue."
